sections.h2: What does the Callaway County Recorder of Deeds do?
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds keeps the public record of land transactions for the county, so a house sale in Callaway County is not complete until the deed is filed there. The county's Recorder page says the office handles deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, surveys, plats, affidavits, marriage licenses, military discharges and tax liens.

Christine Kleindienst holds the office. The office is open to public research and keeps transactions in historical order. A seller usually never walks in, since the title company sends the deed over after closing. It still helps to know what the office will and will not accept, because a rejected deed can hold up your payoff.

If you own a house in the Kingdom of Callaway and are weighing a quick as-is sale, the recorded deed is the last step of that sale. Cash Home Buyers can tell you what the title company will need from the recorder before the closing date is set.

sections.h2: Where is the Callaway County Recorder's office and when is it open?
sections.html:
It is in the Historic Courthouse in Fulton, the county seat. The county lists the details below.

  • Address: 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251
  • Telephone: 573-642-0787
  • Fax: 573-642-1491
  • Hours: 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with the register closing at 4:00 p.m. (new hours took effect on July 17, 2023)

The register closing at 4:00 matters on a closing day. A deed that reaches the counter at 4:15 will most likely be recorded the next business day, so ask the title company which day the paperwork will be submitted. The same courthouse holds the Collector, Assessor and County Clerk, which makes one trip enough for most questions about a property.

sections.h2: What is Callaway County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Callaway County sits north of the Missouri River, across from Jefferson City, and covers about 835 square miles of land. Wikipedia describes the northern part as flat with few large forests, while the southern edge along the river is heavily forested hills and valleys. Cedar Creek forms most of the western border. The county is part of the Jefferson City metropolitan area, and Fulton is the county seat.

The county was organized on November 25, 1820, and the first county seat was Elizabeth. It is also called the Kingdom of Callaway, a nickname from the Civil War era when local leaders arranged a ceasefire with Union troops. German immigrants who arrived from the 1830s on planted the vineyards that later returned as wineries. The Callaway Nuclear Generating Station stands near Fulton.

Cities in the county include Auxvasse, Fulton, Holts Summit, Mokane and New Bloomfield, with part of Jefferson City on the south side. Public school districts that reach into the county include Fulton 58, North Callaway County R-I, South Callaway County R-II, New Bloomfield R-III, Community R-VI and Jefferson City Public Schools, so the district named on a deed's tax bill is worth checking before you list.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Callaway County?
sections.html:
Missouri law sets the recorder's own fee at $5 for the first page and $3 for each page after it, and a statewide increase of $2 under Senate Bill 938 began on August 28, 2026. Total charges at the counter are higher than the $5 figure, because other statutory fees are added to every instrument.

As a guide, the Cole County Recorder's published schedule shows $26 for the first page of a standard document and $3 for each additional page, and Camden County lists the same $26 and $3. Call the Callaway Recorder at 573-642-0787 and ask for the fee sheet in force today. Other charges in RSMo 59.310 include:

  • $5 for each extra item when one document releases or assigns more than one item
  • $25 extra when a document does not meet the format rules
  • $1 for a certificate and seal, and up to $2 for the first copied page plus $1 for later pages
  • $25 per sheet to record a subdivision plat, and $5 per sheet for a survey of one or more tracts

The statute's fee list has no line for a transfer tax or a charge based on the sale price, so a deed is billed by page count and document type. Your title company will total the recording charge on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What format must a deed have to be recorded in Callaway County?
sections.html:
The Recorder can refuse a document that fails the layout rules in RSMo 59.310, so the title company or attorney who prepares your deed has to follow them. The main rules are short.

  • Pages are printed on one side only, not bound, on white or light paper of at least twenty-pound weight.
  • Type is no smaller than eight point, in black or dark ink, and clear enough to copy.
  • The top margin is at least three inches, kept free for the recorder's certification, and all other margins are at least three-fourths of an inch.
  • Signatures are in dark ink with the name typed or printed beneath.

Below the three-inch margin on page one, the deed must show its title, its date, every grantor's name and marital status, every grantee's name, any statutory addresses and the legal description. Documents that miss these rules can still be recorded for the added $25 fee. Deeds signed before January 1, 2002, certified copies and documents signed outside the United States are exempt from the format rules.

A rejected document comes back to the person who submitted it with a written reason, so a mistake costs time more than money.

sections.h2: How do I search Callaway County land records?
sections.html:
You can view recorded documents online at callawaymo.icounty.com. The Recorder's page says printing is available through subscriptions at several levels, and you can call the office for the options. The page also points to DeedWatch, a notification service run by the county's records vendor, which can alert an owner when a new document is recorded under their name.

That alert is useful for a seller who has inherited a house or who shares a title with a relative, because it shows a lien, a release or a new deed soon after it is filed. It is also one way to spot a filing you did not expect before a buyer's title company does.

The county also offers free GIS maps for the public, listed on its home page, which help with parcel lines on rural lots outside Fulton.

sections.h2: Which other Callaway County offices matter when I sell?
sections.html:
Three offices share the courthouse at 10 E. 5th Street and open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

  • The Collector, Sarah Gladman, at 573-642-0747, bills and takes property tax payments. The county FAQ says tax statements go out in the last week of October.
  • The Assessor, Jody Paschal, values more than 26,000 parcels. Real property calls go to 573-642-0768, and personal property to 573-642-0766.
  • The County Clerk handles Board of Equalization appeals.

The Assessor's page says field crews gather data in marked vehicles, wear safety vests with body cameras and county ID, and knock first. They take outside photos, may ask about a finished basement or the number of bathrooms, and never ask to come inside. Missouri law sets an appeal deadline for the Board of Equalization at the second Monday in July, and the Assessor's page for 2026 named July 8 at 5 p.m., so ask the Clerk for the exact date each year.

If a house has back taxes or an open lien, tell the title company early so the payoff is on the first settlement draft.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Callaway County?
faqs.a: At the Recorder of Deeds, 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. with the register closing at 4:00 p.m. Call 573-642-0787 to check how to submit it, since recording by mail is a common route for title companies.

faqs.q: How much is the Callaway County recording fee?
faqs.a: Missouri's statute sets $5 for the first page and $3 for each added page, plus other statutory fees and a $2 statewide increase that began August 28, 2026. Other counties post $26 for a first page, so ask the Callaway Recorder for the current sheet.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Callaway County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Recorded documents can be viewed at callawaymo.icounty.com, and the Recorder sells subscriptions if you want to print them. The office can also explain what each level includes.

faqs.q: Why would the Recorder reject my deed?
faqs.a: The usual reasons are format problems under RSMo 59.310: a margin smaller than three inches at the top of page one, small or faint type, signatures without printed names, or missing grantor and grantee details. The office sends the document back with a written reason.

faqs.q: Does Callaway County charge a transfer tax on a house sale?
faqs.a: The recorder fee list in RSMo 59.310 has no transfer tax line, only fees by page and by document type. Ask the Recorder at 573-642-0787 or your title company to confirm the total for your deed.
